title: Forces and Equilibrium Module 5 Lesson 3: Rough Incline Applied Force Ranges custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A block of mass $5\text{ kg}$ ($W = 50\text{ N}$) rests on a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.2$. A force of magnitude $P$ acts up the line of greatest slope. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the range of values of $P$ for which the block remains in equilibrium.

A block of mass $4\text{ kg}$ ($W = 40\text{ N}$) is on a rough plane inclined at $20^\circ$ to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.5$. A force $P$ acts up the line of greatest slope. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, explain why the block can remain at rest with $P = 0$, and find the maximum force $P_{\max}$ before the block moves up the slope.

A block $A$ of mass $8\text{ kg}$ ($W_A = 80\text{ N}$) on a rough slope inclined at $30^\circ$ with $\mu = 0.25$ is connected via a light string over a smooth pulley to a hanging mass $m$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the range of values of $m$ for which block $A$ remains in equilibrium.

A parcel of mass $10\text{ kg}$ ($W = 100\text{ N}$) is on a rough slope of $30^\circ$ with $\mu = 0.4$. A force $P = 60\text{ N}$ acts up the line of greatest slope. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the actual friction force $F_f$ acting on the parcel and state its direction.

A crate of mass $6\text{ kg}$ ($W = 60\text{ N}$) rests on a rough plane inclined at $15^\circ$ to the horizontal with $\mu = 0.6$. A force $Q$ is applied directed down the line of greatest slope. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the maximum value of $Q$ before the crate starts sliding down the plane.

A block of mass $5\text{ kg}$ ($W = 50\text{ N}$) is on a rough plane inclined at $45^\circ$ with $\mu = 0.2$. A horizontal force $P$ pushes into the plane. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the minimum and maximum values of $P$ to maintain equilibrium.

questions.prompt: A block of mass $m = 15\text{ kg}$ ($W = 150\text{ N}$) rests on a rough plane inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal, where $\tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}$ (so $\sin\alpha = 0.6$ and $\cos\alpha = 0.8$). The coefficient of friction between the block and the plane is $\mu = 0.3$. A force of magnitude $P$ acts up the line of greatest slope. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving perpendicular to the inclined plane, calculate the normal reaction $R$ and the maximum possible frictional force $F_{\max}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the minimum force $P_{\min}$ and the maximum force $P_{\max}$ for equilibrium, and state the range of values of $P$ for which the block remains at rest.

questions.prompt: A particle $A$ of mass $m_A = 10\text{ kg}$ ($W_A = 100\text{ N}$) is on a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal with coefficient of friction $\mu = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{5} \approx 0.3464$. A light string attached to $A$ passes over a smooth pulley at the top of the incline and supports a vertically hanging mass $m_B$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that the maximum static friction force that can act on particle $A$ is $30\text{ N}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Determine the range of values of $m_B$ for which particle $A$ remains in equilibrium.

questions.prompt: A crate of mass $m = 20\text{ kg}$ ($W = 200\text{ N}$) rests on a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction between the crate and the plane is $\mu = 0.2$. A force of magnitude $T$ is applied at an angle of $30^\circ$ above the line of greatest slope. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: When the crate is on the point of sliding down the plane, express the normal reaction $R$ and the limiting friction $F_1$ in terms of $T$, and calculate the minimum pulling force $T_{\min}$ correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: If the pulling force $T$ is increased until the crate is on the point of sliding up the plane, calculate the maximum pulling force $T_{\max}$ correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A particle of mass $m = 6\text{ kg}$ ($W = 60\text{ N}$) is on a rough plane inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal, where $\tan\alpha = \frac{7}{24}$ (so $\sin\alpha = 0.28$ and $\cos\alpha = 0.96$). The coefficient of friction between the particle and the plane is $\mu = 0.25$. A horizontal force of magnitude $P$ acts in the vertical plane containing the line of greatest slope. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces parallel and perpendicular to the inclined plane, calculate the minimum horizontal force $P_{\min}$ required to prevent the particle from sliding down the slope correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum horizontal force $P_{\max}$ before the particle starts sliding up the plane correct to 3 significant figures, and state the range of values of $P$ for equilibrium.

questions.prompt: A block $A$ of mass $5\text{ kg}$ on a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal with $\mu_A = 0.4$ is connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth pulley at the top of the slope to a block $B$ of mass $M$ resting on a rough horizontal surface with $\mu_B = 0.5$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum friction force $F_{A,\max}$ on block $A$, and express the maximum friction force $F_{B,\max}$ on block $B$ in terms of $M$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: If block $A$ is in limiting equilibrium on the point of sliding down the slope, calculate the minimum mass $M_{\min}$ of block $B$ required correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: If an additional external force of $60\text{ N}$ pulls block $A$ up the line of greatest slope, calculate the minimum mass $M'$ of block $B$ needed to prevent the system from moving up the slope.

questions.prompt: A crate of mass $m = 10\text{ kg}$ ($W = 100\text{ N}$) rests on a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction between the crate and the plane is $\mu = 0.4$. A force of magnitude $P$ acts at an angle $\theta$ to the line of greatest slope. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: If the force acts parallel to the line of greatest slope ($\theta = 0$), calculate the minimum holding force $P_{\min}$ and the maximum holding force $P_{\max}$, and state the complete range of values of $P$ for equilibrium.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: If the force is applied at an angle $\theta$ above the line of greatest slope ($0^\circ \leqslant \theta < 60^\circ$) to pull the crate up the plane, show that the pulling force is minimized when $\tan\theta = \mu = 0.4$, and calculate the minimum force $P_{\min,\text{up}}$ and the corresponding normal reaction $R$.

questions.prompt: A fixed rough wedge has two symmetrical faces each inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. Block $A$ of mass $m_A = 6\text{ kg}$ rests on the left face with $\mu_A = 0.3$. Block $B$ of mass $m_B$ rests on the right face with $\mu_B = 0.4$. The blocks are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth pulley at the apex. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum friction forces $F_{A,\max}$ and $F_{B,\max}$ that can act on each face in terms of the respective masses.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: If the system is in limiting equilibrium on the point of slipping towards block $A$ (block $A$ sliding down, block $B$ sliding up), calculate the minimum mass $m_{B,\min}$ required correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: If instead block $B$ is on the point of sliding down its face (pulling block $A$ up), calculate the maximum mass $m_{B,\max}$ of block $B$ correct to 3 significant figures, and state the complete range of values of $m_B$ for equilibrium.
